title: Conditional Expressions and Choosing Between Alternatives
learningObjectives: Explain how a conditional expression selects one of two values based on a Boolean condition.
Write a ternary expression using condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse.
Trace a ternary expression and predict its result.
Choose when a ternary expression is clearer than an if/else statement.
Avoid confusing, deeply nested ternary expressions and common syntax mistakes.

understand.concept: A conditional expression evaluates a condition and produces one of two values. In JavaScript, the ternary operator is written condition ? expressionIfTrue : expressionIfFalse. The condition is evaluated first. If it is truthy, the expression after ? is selected; otherwise the expression after : is selected. Only the selected expression is evaluated.
understand.whyItMatters: Some decisions produce a value that will be stored, displayed, passed to a function, or used in another expression. A conditional expression can make a small two-choice decision concise without creating a separate multi-line if/else statement.
understand.analogy: A sign says, 'If the door is open, use the entrance; otherwise use the side entrance.' The condition determines which one of two choices is selected.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy gives two choices, but real code expressions can compute values, have side effects, or contain complex logic. Keep ternary branches simple and avoid hiding important actions inside them.

explain.narrative: The ternary operator is the only JavaScript operator that takes three operands: a condition, the value expression chosen when the condition is truthy, and the value expression chosen when it is falsy. Its form is condition ? valueA : valueB. It is an expression, so it can be assigned to a variable or used where a value is expected. It is not a replacement for every if/else statement. Prefer if/else when branches perform multiple statements, when the decision has several outcomes, or when a ternary becomes difficult to scan. Parentheses can clarify complex conditions. Avoid nesting ternary operators unless the result remains immediately understandable.

examples.title: Select a message
examples.code: const isReady = true;\nconst message = isReady ? 'Ready' : 'Please wait';\nconsole.log(message);
examples.explanation: The condition is true, so the expression produces the first value, 'Ready', which is assigned to message.

examples.title: Choose a numeric value
examples.explanation: The total is below 500, so the false branch supplies the shipping amount of 50.

examples.title: Use a ternary inside output
examples.explanation: The selected string becomes the argument passed to console.log.

examples.title: Return a selected value from a function
examples.explanation: The function returns one of two values based on its parameter. A ternary is compact here because each branch is a simple value.

examples.title: Prefer if/else for multiple actions
examples.explanation: This example intentionally uses if/else because the true branch contains two statements. Using a ternary here would not improve clarity.

commonMistakes: Leaving out the colon that separates the two choices.
Using assignment (=) instead of comparison (===) in the condition.
Putting statements that do not produce a useful value into a ternary just to shorten code.
Nesting ternary operators until the decision becomes difficult to read.
Assuming both branches are evaluated; only the selected branch is evaluated.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Display a payment status
guidedTask.instructions: Create a conditional expression that assigns 'Paid' when paymentReceived is true and 'Pending' otherwise. Print the resulting status.
steps: Use the condition ? 'Paid' : 'Pending' to select a value.
Assign the selected value to status.
Print status and change the Boolean to test both outcomes.

independentTask.title: Independent: Ticket price label
independentTask.instructions: Select a label for a ticket based on whether the visitor is under 12. If under 12, select 'Child ticket'; otherwise select 'Regular ticket'. Use a ternary expression for the value selection, print it, and test both outcomes.
requirements: Use a Boolean condition or age comparison.
Produce exactly the two specified labels.
Store the selected label in a variable.
Test the true and false outcomes.
Then rewrite the same decision using if/else and compare readability.

hints: Read the condition before the question mark.
The expression before the colon is selected when the condition is truthy.
The expression after the colon is selected when the condition is falsy.
A ternary expression produces a value; it can be assigned or returned.
Keep both choices short and easy to understand.
If branches contain multiple actions or the expression is nested, consider if/else for clarity.

questions.prompt: What does the ternary operator do?
options: Selects one of two expressions based on a condition
Repeats a block until a condition changes
questions.answer: Selects one of two expressions based on a condition
questions.explanation: The condition determines which of the two expressions supplies the resulting value.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct ternary structure?
questions.explanation: The ternary form uses a question mark followed by the true expression and a colon followed by the false expression.

questions.prompt: What is assigned by this code: const label = 8 > 5 ? 'Yes' : 'No';
questions.explanation: The condition 8 > 5 is true, so the first expression is selected.

questions.prompt: When is if/else usually clearer than a ternary expression?
options: When branches contain multiple statements or the decision is complex
Only when the condition is false
questions.answer: When branches contain multiple statements or the decision is complex
questions.explanation: Use if/else for multi-step branches and decisions that are hard to read in a single expression.

options: Keep branches simple and avoid unnecessary nesting
Nest as many ternaries as possible
Put unrelated actions in both branches
questions.answer: Keep branches simple and avoid unnecessary nesting
questions.explanation: Simple branches make the expression easy to scan and reduce mistakes.
